chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a boy and a girl whom their guardians married while they were not yet mature (minor), so he said: 'The marriage is valid, and whichever of them reaches maturity has the option (to annul or confirm). If they both die before reaching maturity, there is no inheritance between them, nor is there a dowry, unless they had both reached maturity and consented.' I said: 'What if one of them reaches maturity before the other?' He said: 'That is valid upon him if he consents.' I said: 'If the man who reached maturity before the girl consented to the marriage, then he died before the girl reached maturity, do I inherit him?' He said: 'Yes, her inheritance is set aside from him until she reaches maturity, then she swears by Allah that nothing prompted her to take the inheritance except her consent to the marriage, then the inheritance and half the dowry are given to her.' I said: 'If the girl died and had not yet reached maturity, does the mature husband inherit her?' He said: 'No, because she has the option if she reaches maturity.' I said: 'If her father was the one who married her before she reached maturity?' He said: 'The father's marriage is valid upon her, and it is valid upon the boy, and the dowry is upon the father for the girl.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if a man contracted marriage for his daughter while she was a minor to a young boy who had not yet reached maturity, and the one who managed the contract for the boy was his father, then if one of the two minors died, his partner (the other minor) inherits him.

key_terms.اَلْخِيَار: The right of option/choice to annul or confirm a contract upon reaching maturity

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of inheritance and validity for the marriage of minors in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of *nikah* for minors under the guardianship of their parents or guardians, establishing that while the contract is binding, the minor retains the right of option (*khiyar*) upon reaching maturity. It provides detailed jurisprudential rulings on inheritance and dowry (*mahr*) in cases where one spouse dies before the other attains maturity, highlighting the Shia principle that the surviving minor must confirm the marriage to claim inheritance. The text further distinguishes the financial responsibilities of the father when he acts as the contracting guardian for his daughter.
